title: Redwood discovery - reliability & multi-region fallbacks with Vela Finance
summary: Initial reliability and incident-tolerance discovery. Vela runs customer-facing chat and transaction assistant; primary concerns are multi-region failover, SLA guarantees, and data residency. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, fallbacks to cheaper models/regions, KMS and audit log needs, and proposed pilot + benchmark run next week.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to share dedicated pricing sheet and Hosted SLA details (Carlos) - due 2027-01-12
SE to run a short benchmark template and propose test harness (Priya) - due 2027-01-15
Customer to confirm pilot scope and expected traffic patterns (Maya) - due 2027-01-11
Schedule technical deep dive on VPC/private deployment options (tentative week of 2027-01-18)
action_items: Carlos Mendez: Send dedicated pricing + Hosted SLA PDF (due 2027-01-12)
Priya Shah: Prepare benchmark plan & data collection checklist (due 2027-01-15)
Maya Patel: Provide sample traffic profile + PII/data residency constraints (due 2027-01-11)
Samir Rao: Share internal incident runbook and current failover tests (optional)
transcript: [00:00] Carlos Mendez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Carlos, AE at Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Maya Patel: Good, thanks. Maya here. We're eager to understand how Redwood handles outages and cross-region failovers for our transaction assistant.
[00:15] Carlos Mendez: Great. Quick agenda: understand your current infra, pain points on incidents, SLOs, and run through Hosted/Dedicated/Private tradeoffs and fallback options.

[00:30] Jared Kim: Sounds good. I'll give a quick background: Vela handles around 1200 reqs/sec at peak, global traffic split US/EU/APAC. Latency SLO is 200ms p50 for chat flows, cost sensitivity on token spend is high.

[00:45] Priya Shah: Thanks Jared. Two immediate flags: multi-region routing and how you want to handle failures — do you prefer region-to-region failover with same model, or fallback to smaller/cheaper model in another region?

[01:05] Samir Rao: Ideally, we'd prefer region-to-region with the same model to keep quality, but willing to accept a degraded cheaper model for short windows to preserve availability. How does Redwood manage that?

[01:20] Priya Shah: We support policy-based routing. You can define primary region and failover priorities. On capacity or region outage, traffic can be routed to a compatible variant (same architecture/quantization) or a smaller model. There are automated rules and a manual override. We also do health checks and traffic steering via topology-aware controllers.
[01:45] Maya Patel: Health checks—are those at the model endpoint level or infra level? We have strict SLOs and need observability into what failed.

[01:55] Priya Shah: Both. We run per-route health probes, per-node metrics, and synthetic user journeys. All of that surfaces in Redwood Console with traces and per-token latency breakdowns. We retain traces for X days depending on plan — can provide retention options.
[02:15] Jared Kim: SLA question: for Hosted, what's the uptime SLA and the credit policy? Also, for Dedicated we need throughput guarantees per reserved pool.

[02:28] Carlos Mendez: Hosted standard SLA is 99.9% availability for inference APIs with targeted latencies; Dedicated has an SLA aligned to reserved capacity and throughput commitments (we can share exact numbers in the pricing doc). For mission-critical we recommend Dedicated or Private so you can isolate capacity and get stronger guarantees.
[02:45] Maya Patel: And Private — is that fully on-prem or VPC? How much control do we get over networking and KMS?

[02:55] Priya Shah: Private has two flavors: VPC hosted control plane with customer-managed networking and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. KMS integrations supported (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options). You get audit log access, SAML SSO, RBAC, and ability to control data egress policies.
[03:15] Samir Rao: For compliance we need SOC 2 type II and detailed audit logs per request. Does Redwood provide per-request audit trails and raw logs?

[03:25] Priya Shah: Yes, audit logs are available and we can stream them to your SIEM. We also have request-level metadata, anonymized payload retention options, and a compliance package for longer retention and audit support.
[03:40] Jared Kim: During an incident, what's the typical time to failover? And do you have automated canary rollbacks?

[03:50] Priya Shah: Failover time depends on routing and DNS TTLs; within our platform, once a region is marked unhealthy, routing shifts within seconds to tens of seconds at the load balancer level. If you need sub-second, we can discuss fronting with CDN-level routing. For deployments, we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback based on error/latency thresholds.
[04:15] Maya Patel: We're also concerned about cold-starts when failing over to a new region and model warming. Any caching or KV reuse?

[04:26] Priya Shah: We have automatic prefix/KV caching and a warmup mechanism for commonly used prompts. When a failover occurs, cached KV is region-scoped, but we can pre-warm fallback replicas and keep a warmed standby if you opt for dedicated pools.

[04:45] Carlos Mendez: Quick interjection — on cost tradeoffs: fallback to smaller models or quantized variants reduces cost but can reduce generation quality. Many customers set policy like: 0–5 min keep trying same model, 5–60 min fallback to X-quantized variant, and set quality thresholds.
[05:05] Samir Rao: Interesting. Can we run a regression test to measure user-facing quality difference?

[05:12] Priya Shah: Absolutely. We recommend a prompt set eval suite — we'll run it across model variants during the pilot to measure latency/cost vs quality regressions and tie alerts to quality deltas.
[05:28] Jared Kim: About multi-region, do you support active-active or active-passive?

[05:36] Priya Shah: Both. Active-active routing needs model replication and consistent KV cache strategy; we support asynchronous KV replication or client-side sticky sessions. Active-passive is simpler and common for cost reasons.
[05:50] Maya Patel: If we go Hosted initially but need to move to Private later for compliance, how painful is migration?

[05:58] Carlos Mendez: We designed the API and deployment configs to be portable. You can pin model versions and rollout policies; moving from Hosted to Dedicated/Private is mostly a control-plane and network configuration change. We'll provide migration runbooks and a migration support lane.
[06:15] Samir Rao: Any limits around region-to-region data residency? We have EU data residency requirements for some customers.

[06:24] Priya Shah: Yes — you can route EU traffic to EU-only models and regionally isolate storage. For Private, you can enforce that data never leaves certain regions. We'll document where logs and backups live.
[06:40] Jared Kim: Let's talk incident comp/credits — if Dedicated's throughput fails, what are remedies?

[06:49] Carlos Mendez: For Dedicated, the contract includes remediation: capacity scaling, priority scheduling on Redwood capacity, and financial credits proportional to SLA breach. We'll include exact terms in the dedicated contract template.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Do you provide runbooks or war-room support for high-sev incidents?
[07:12] Carlos Mendez: Yes, enterprise tier includes dedicated escalation paths, on-call mobilization with our SREs, and collaborative incident response. We'll map our contacts in the contract.

[07:30] Priya Shah: On fallback policy examples — one customer had an automated fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant that preserved coherence for 95% of prompts; they used that for up to 10 minutes before DR teams engaged. We can share anonymized reference patterns.
[07:50] Jared Kim: Could we see logs of a previous failover for reference? Not PII, just metrics and timeline.
[07:58] Priya Shah: We can share redacted incident timelines and metrics; I'll add that to the follow-ups.
[08:10] Maya Patel: For the pilot, we want to simulate a region outage and see routing/fallback behavior and user impact. Can Redwood help orchestrate that?

[08:19] Priya Shah: Yes — SE team can help set up a chaos test harness in a staging environment and run through failure scenarios, measure latency and quality. We'll instrument synthetic traffic to match your production distribution.
[08:35] Samir Rao: How do you handle model state — session continuity during failover? Our assistants keep some KV state per session.

[08:43] Priya Shah: Session-level KV is sticky to region; for critical continuity we recommend active-active replication or client-side state sync. For short failovers, you can accept slight session degradation or rehydrate state from a shared store.
[09:00] Jared Kim: Any special networking requirements for Private? Firewalls, peering, egress rules?

[09:07] Priya Shah: Private deployments require VPC peering, specific firewall rules, and optional NAT configurations. We'll provide a deployment network checklist. For on-prem, there's an appliance and orchestration playbook.
[09:25] Maya Patel: Regarding metrics, we need per-route p50/p95/p99 and token cost breakdown by user segment. Is that out of the box?
[09:33] Priya Shah: Yes — Redwood Console has per-route latency percentiles and token-level cost breakdowns. You can tag routes by customer segment and apply dashboards, and export to your BI.

[09:50] Carlos Mendez: Let's capture concrete success criteria: 1) maintain 200ms p50 under normal load, 2) <2s p95 under failover with acceptable quality, 3) documented incident runbook and audit logs. Does that align?
[10:05] Maya Patel: Yes. Also add data residency and SOC2 compliance as must-haves.
[10:12] Carlos Mendez: Noted. We'll send pricing, SLA docs, and a benchmark template. Priya will prepare a pilot plan and a staging chaos test.
[10:22] Jared Kim: One last question — for fallback models, how do you validate hallucination rates?
10:28] Priya Shah: We run prompt-set based evals and track hallucination/regression metrics; during pilot we'll run those comparisons and tie alerts to threshold breaches.
[10:45] Maya Patel: Great. Thanks. Looking forward to the docs and the pilot plan.
[10:50] Carlos Mendez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing + security packet and schedule the deep technical session. Action items recap coming in email.
[10:58] Meeting ended
